correctness.rationale: The triple has gcd one: a+c−2b=3 while a and b are consecutive residues modulo 3. I symbolically expanded the area identity and all eighteen claimed weighted congruence reductions in review-evidence/checks.py (argument 4, SymPy). Substituting n=48+r+6j verifies integer affine coefficients with the required positivity and order on every residue branch, not just at samples. The three outside corners generate the complement of the staircase; each reduction preserves the residue, keeps the coordinates nonnegative and lowers the positive weight. Every residue has a nonnegative expression in b,c modulo a by gcd one, and hence reduces to the staircase. Its cardinality a forces exactly one pair per residue. Adding an a-generator cannot lower the value, so the staircase gives the full Apéry set. The two corner weights suffice for the maximum; their winning differences have positive coefficients in j on all branches, and the winning weights minus a expand to the displayed cubics. A separate shortest-path computation in the review script compares the entire Apéry set at two arguments per class. Those finite checks are corroboration; the identities and descent prove the universal claim. The supplied verifier was read, not run.

value.rationale: Consecutive ordinary pentagonal generators are a natural established test family, with a published sequence but no uniform formula in that entry. The branch distinctions and finite cutoff are explicit; the full staircase also answers every minimal-residue query without rerunning a search on roughly n² residues. This is materially stronger than eventual existence or another finite tabulation and does not depend on 48 being optimal.
